note: Not_deconditioned is the strongest match available — a thirteen-year soldier who has just completed Ranger School and is three months from Regiment selection is the furthest possible point from the stated exclusion. Good_to_great also matches in shape: he is not seeking rescue, he is rebuilding from a temporary and deliberate depletion back toward an elite standard, with a specific performance target attached. He misses on successful as the criterion is literally written — 'business owner, physician or equivalent' does not map onto a career soldier, though this is the clearest case in the batch where the wording rather than the intent produces the miss, and the rollup may want to revisit whether the criterion is describing income bracket or accomplishment. Neglected_health is an unambiguous miss and it is the one that actually decided this call: health is not his neglected area, it is his profession. He trains almost daily, has unit-assigned strength and nutrition coaches, and has free gym access. Income is deliberately omitted from both lists because it was never tested — the one-to-one offer was never formally presented, only a vague 'roughly from $4,000 to $9,000' band, and no financial question was asked, so there is no basis to score affordability either way. Read alongside the Hamdi Hmimy call the same day, this is the second instance of the same pattern: a prospect who passes the physical and aspirational criteria comfortably and fails on need, and the ICP as written has no way to see that coming before the call is booked.
